question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 04 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The increase in p95 latency is due to a reduction in the database pool size, leading to connection exhaustion.
why_chain: The database pool size was reduced from 50 to 5, causing the connection pool to be exhausted more frequently.
This reduction in pool size means fewer connections are available to service checkout requests.
As a result, more checkout requests are waiting for a free connection, leading to increased latency.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in p95 latency is also due to the increase in error rate, indicating more checkout requests are failing.
why_chain: The error rate for checkout requests increased from 0.46% to 0.70% after the change.
More checkout requests are failing, which contributes to the overall p95 latency increase.
Failed requests add to the overall latency, as they require retries and additional processing time.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a sudden increase in request volume.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for checkout did not change significantly (15% increase).

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a change in traffic patterns.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a sudden increase in traffic or a campaign that could explain the change.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a failure or slowdown in any external service.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to an infrastructure issue.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of any network or server capacity issues.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a configuration change unrelated to the database pool size.
ruled_out.reason: The database pool size change is the only configuration change that occurred around the time of the change point.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in p95 latency is due to a logging issue.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of any logging issues or changes in logging configuration.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for service checkout rose from 220 ms to 638 ms (+190%), with a change point at 2026-03-04T04:55:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service checkout: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for service checkout stayed about the same (819 per 5 min before, 940 per 5 min after, +15%).
At the same time, error rate for service checkout rose (0.46% before, 0.70% after, +51%).
Changed checkout db.pool_size from 50 to 5 (all regions) (checkout; 1 min before the change; record R009)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, us-east; 2 min after the change; record R010)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, eu-west; 3 min after the change; record R011)
p95 latency above SLO on checkout (checkout; 15 min after the change; record R013)
checkout: WARN connection pool exhausted, waiting for a free connection (checkout, ap-south; 7 min after the change; record R012)

reasons: ✓ A change event (config_changes) lines up in time (1 min before the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Increase the database pool size to a higher value to prevent connection exhaustion.
Monitor the error rate for checkout requests and take corrective action if it continues to rise.
Review and optimize the checkout process to reduce the number of failed requests.
